title: Refusal
description: The body of a refusal the control plane answers an adapter's request with, application/json. The codes an adapter meets: 401 unauthorized, the same whatever the cause, and never taken as the access key being revoked: an unknown or revoked access key, a key of another kind, a bad signature, a GET's X-Qory-Timestamp or a POST's time more than 300 seconds from the control plane's clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, under the replay rule of definitions.schema.json; 403 forbidden, a request outside the access key's rights; 400 bad_request, a signing header that is missing, malformed or sent twice, X-Qory-Instance-Id among them, other than a missing X-Qory-Contract-Version, which is unsupported_contract_version; 400 unsupported_contract_version, an X-Qory-Contract-Version the control plane does not serve; 400 invalid_request, a body that breaks its schema; 404 not_found, a route the control plane does not serve; 413 payload_too_large, a request over 1 MiB; 415 unsupported_media_type, a request that is not application/json; 409 collection_not_linked, items of a collection that is not linked to a workspace; 429 rate_limited, with Retry-After, the seconds the adapter waits before it sends the request again, built anew, as definitions.schema.json describes a retry. A 401, 413, 415 or 400 bad_request may be unsigned, because the control plane may decide them before it verifies the request's signature. Every other answer is signed, and an adapter acts on no other unsigned answer. A signed answer is signed as definitions.schema.json describes. A member this schema does not define is refused.
